hcontainer.heading: Digital asset platforms and tokenised custody platforms

content.p: Insert:

section.heading: Meaning of digital token

content.p: (1) A digital token is:
an electronic record that one or more persons are capable of factually controlling as described in subsection (2); or
an electronic record prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph;
but does not include an electronic record that, under the regulations, is prescribed not to be a digital token.
Note: The regulations may prescribe a class of electronic record (see subsection 13(3) of the Legislation Act 2003).
When a person is capable of factually controlling an electronic record
(2) A person is capable of factually controlling an electronic record if the person can (whether alone or jointly with one or more other persons):
transfer the electronic record; and
exclude one or more other persons from transferring the electronic record; and
demonstrate that the person can do the things in paragraphs (a) and (b).
Note: A person who can do all of these things possesses the digital token (see paragraph 86(2)(a)).
In working out whether a person can do a thing in paragraph (2)(a), (b) or (c):
it only matters what the person can do as a matter of fact rather than law; and
it does not matter if another person can also do that thing.
Note 1: An example of when an electronic record is a digital token is if:
the electronic record is created by a payment provider on a distributed ledger to identify a person entitled to withdraw money; and
the person transfers the money by transferring the electronic record to another person, who the provider then recognises as entitled to withdraw the money.
Note 2: An example of when an electronic record is a digital token is if:
the electronic record is created by a custodian on a distributed ledger to identify a person with beneficial ownership of property; and
the person transfers the property by transferring the electronic record to another person, who the provider then recognises as a beneficial owner of the property.
Note 3: An example of when an electronic record is not a digital token is if:
the electronic record is in a ledger maintained by a bank to record a specific account holder’s balance of money that can be withdrawn; and
a transfer of money is effected by the bank altering the electronic record to reflect an updated balance, but not by transferring the electronic record itself.
Note 4: An example of when an electronic record is not a digital token is if:
the electronic record is in a database maintained by a custodian to identify a client with beneficial ownership of property; and
a transfer of the property is effected by the custodian altering the electronic record to reflect the new beneficial owner, but not by transferring the electronic record itself.

section.heading: Meaning of digital asset platform

content.p: (1) A digital asset platform is a facility under which:
(a) a person (the operator) possesses one or more digital tokens (the underlying assets); and
the underlying assets are so possessed for or on behalf of another person, including by the operator:
acting as trustee or bailee; or
being obliged to ensure that the underlying assets are dealt with on the instructions of the other person.
Note 1: Paragraph (a) can be satisfied if an agent of the operator possesses the underlying assets, because the operator is taken to have done anything that the agent does (see subsection 761GE(2)).
Note 2: The operator is the issuer of the platform (see section 761E).
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b), the other person must be a client under the facility or a nominee of such a client.
The facility may also authorise the operator or one or more other persons to engage in conduct:
in relation to an underlying asset; and
for or on behalf of the client or the client nominee.
(4) Despite subsection (1), a tokenised custody platform cannot be a digital asset platform.

section.heading: Meaning of tokenised custody platform

content.p: (1) A tokenised custody platform is a facility under which:
(a) a person (the operator) identifies one or more assets other than money (the underlying assets); and
for each underlying asset:
the operator creates a single digital token; and
possessing the digital token confers a right to redeem, or direct the delivery of, the underlying asset; and
the operator holds each underlying asset; and
each underlying asset is so held for or on behalf of another person who possesses the digital token for the underlying asset, including by the operator:
acting as trustee or bailee; or
being obliged to ensure that the underlying asset is dealt with on the instructions of the other person.
Note 1: Paragraph (c) can be satisfied if an agent of the operator holds the underlying asset, because the operator is taken to have done anything that the agent does (see subsection 761GE(2)).
Note 2: The operator is the issuer of the platform (see section 761E).
The facility may also authorise the operator or one or more other persons to engage in conduct in relation to an underlying asset for, or on behalf of, a person who:
possesses the digital token for the underlying asset; and
is a client under the facility.

Note: If a person is not the first to possess a digital token, merely possessing the digital token does not make the person a client under the facility. For a facility that is an arrangement, the person would need to enter into the arrangement as a client under the facility (see item 5 of the table in subsection 761E(3)).
In this section:
holds: for a digital token, a person holds the digital token if the person possesses the digital token.

section.heading: Agents appointed by operators of digital asset platforms or tokenised custody platforms

content.p: This section applies if the operator of a facility appoints an agent to do anything that the operator is authorised to do in connection with the facility.
For the purposes of determining:
whether the facility is a digital asset platform or a tokenised custody platform; and
if the facility is a digital asset platform or a tokenised custody platform:
whether there is a liability to a client under the facility; or
whether this Act has been complied with for the facility; or
whether the platform rules of the facility have been complied with; or
whether the asset-holding standards or the transactional and settlement standards have been complied with for the facility;

the operator is taken to have done (or failed to do) anything that the agent has done (or failed to do) because of the appointment, even if the agent was acting fraudulently or outside the scope of the agent’s authority.
An agent appointed by:
an agent appointed by the operator as described in subsection (1); or
a person who is taken under this subsection to be an agent of the operator;
to do anything that the operator is authorised to do in connection with the facility is taken to be an agent appointed by the operator to do that thing for the purposes of subsections (1) and (2).

Subdivision E—Related matters

section.heading: Disregard redemption rights when working out whether wrapped tokens etc. are financial products

content.p: (1) In this section, a digital token is a wrapped token if possessing the digital token confers a right (the redemption right) to redeem, or direct the delivery of, one of the following (the related asset):
an underlying asset of a tokenised custody platform;
a digital token held through:
decentralised wrapping software; or
public digital token infrastructure;
an asset of a kind prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph.
Disregard the redemption right when working out whether the wrapped token etc. is a financial product
Disregard the redemption right when working out whether the wrapped token is, or whether rights or interests attached to the wrapped token are, a financial product.
However, subsection (2) does not apply if:

where the related asset is a financial product—a person who possesses the wrapped token has rights or interests that are not equivalent to those the person would have if the person held the related asset directly; or
circumstances prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph apply for the wrapped token.
Definitions
In this section:
decentralised wrapping software, for a wrapped token, means software:
through which the wrapped token’s related asset is held; and
that would be a tokenised custody platform if the following things done by the software were instead done by an operator (within the meaning of subsection 761GD(1)):
creating the wrapped token;
holding the related asset for or on behalf of the person who possesses the wrapped token.
holds: for a digital token, a person holds the digital token if the person possesses the digital token.

Subdivision B—Specific limitations

section.heading: Conduct relating to certain platforms is a financial service only if engaged in by, or on behalf of, a constitutionally-covered corporation

content.p: Despite anything in Subdivision A, conduct that:
relates to a digital asset platform, or a tokenised custody platform, that is a financial product only because of paragraph 764A(1)(la) or (lb); and
would, apart from this section, be a financial service (or a kind of financial service);
is a financial service (or a kind of financial service) only if the conduct is engaged in by, or on behalf of, a constitutionally-covered corporation.
Note: Dealing in a financial product is an example of a kind of financial service (see section 766A).
Subdivision C—Related matters

section.heading: Certain services must be provided by constitutionally-covered corporations

content.p: Person providing service directly, and not through a representative etc.
A person contravenes this section if:
(a) the person is providing a service (the applicable service), but not as an agent or representative of any other person; and
the person uses a postal, telegraphic, telephonic or other like service (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution) to provide all or part of the applicable service; and
the applicable service would be a financial service involving:
providing financial product advice relating to a digital asset platform or a tokenised custody platform; or
dealing in a digital asset platform or a tokenised custody platform; or
engaging in conduct relating to a digital asset platform, or a tokenised custody platform, that is conduct of a kind prescribed for the purposes of paragraph 766A(1)(f);
if the person were a constitutionally-covered corporation; and
the person is not a constitutionally-covered corporation.
Note: This section is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).
Person providing service through a representative etc.
A person contravenes this section if:
(a) another person is providing a service (the applicable service) as an agent or representative of the first-mentioned person; and
the other person uses a postal, telegraphic, telephonic or other like service (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution) to provide all or part of the applicable service; and
the applicable service would be a financial service involving:
providing financial product advice relating to a digital asset platform or a tokenised custody platform; or
dealing in a digital asset platform or a tokenised custody platform; or
engaging in conduct relating to a digital asset platform, or a tokenised custody platform, that is conduct of a kind prescribed for the purposes of paragraph 766A(1)(f);
if the first-mentioned person were a constitutionally-covered corporation; and
the first-mentioned person is not a constitutionally-covered corporation.
Note: This section is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).

Subdivision B—Extensions to the meaning of financial market

section.heading: Extension—certain digital asset platforms providing a market for digital tokens that are not financial products

content.p: Minister may extend the meaning of financial market
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, declare that a digital asset platform is a financial market if:
the platform would be a facility to which subsection 767A(1) applies in relation to one or more specified classes of digital tokens if those digital tokens were financial products; and
the platform is operated by, or on behalf of, a constitutionally-covered corporation.
Note 1: While the declaration is in force, the platform is a financial market to the extent that it relates to the digital tokens (see subsection 767A(6)).
Note 2: In making a declaration, the Minister must have regard to the matters in subsection (5).
Note 3: The declaration may declare a class of digital asset platforms (see subsection 13(3) of the Legislation Act 2003).
The declaration may apply:
unconditionally or subject to specified conditions; and
(b) for a specified period or indefinitely (the extension duration).
Varying or revoking an extension
The Minister may, at any time by legislative instrument:
vary a declaration given under subsection (1) to:
impose conditions, or additional conditions, on the declaration; or
vary or revoke any of the conditions on the declaration; or
extend or shorten the extension duration (including as affected by any variation from a previous operation of this subparagraph); or
revoke a declaration given under subsection (1).
However, the Minister may only take action under subsection (3) after:
giving notice, and an opportunity to make submissions on the proposed action, to the operator of each facility known by the Minister to be covered by the declaration; and
both:

the Minister has caused a notice to be published on ASIC’s website allowing a reasonable period within which the operator of each facility covered by the declaration may make submissions on the proposed action; and
that period has ended; and
having regard to the matters in paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) and (5)(a) to (e).
Matters relevant to giving an extension etc.
In considering whether to make a declaration under subsection (1), the Minister must have regard to the following:
the likely effect on the Australian economy, and on the efficiency, integrity and stability of the Australian financial system;
any impact on competition in the operation of financial markets or on the provision of digital asset platforms;
the likely regulatory impact;
whether each facility that could be covered by the declaration has a material connection with this jurisdiction;
any relevant advice the Minister has received under subsection (6).
The Minister may also have regard to any other matters that the Minister considers relevant.
Regulators may advise the Minister
ASIC, APRA, the Reserve Bank or AUSTRAC may (on its own initiative) and must (at the request of the Minister):
consider whether a declaration should be made, varied or revoked under this section; and
advise the Minister accordingly.

section.heading: Meaning of possession

content.p: General (things other than digital tokens)
(1) A thing that is in a person’s custody or under a person’s control is in the person’s possession.
Digital tokens

for an electronic record that is a digital token because of paragraph 761GB(1)(a)—the person is capable of factually controlling the electronic record as described in subsection 761GB(2); or

the person needs the express cooperation of another person in order to be able to satisfy paragraph 761GB(2)(a), (b) or (c) for the electronic record; and

transactional and settlement standards means standards in force under section 912BF.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: After Subdivision A of Division 3 of Part 7.6

content.p: Insert:
Subdivision AA—Specific obligations for financial services businesses involving certain platforms

section.heading: Scope of this Subdivision

content.p: This Subdivision applies in relation to:
a financial services licensee; and
a digital asset platform or a tokenised custody platform;
to the extent that one or more of the financial services authorised by the licence relate to the issuing of the platform.

section.heading: Compliance with standards

content.p: The licensee must comply with the following standards to the extent that the standards relate to the financial services:
the asset-holding standards;
the transactional and settlement standards.
Note 1: This section is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).
Note 2: For the making of these standards, see sections 912BE and 912BF.

section.heading: Having adequate platform rules

content.p: The licensee must have platform rules for the platform that comply with subsection 912BG(1).
Note: This section is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).

section.heading: Compliance with declaration prohibiting transactions etc. involving certain financial products through certain platforms

content.p: The licensee must comply with a prohibition in force under section 912BH relating to the financial services and the platform.
Note: This section is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).

section.heading: Asset-holding standards

content.p: (1) ASIC may, by legislative instrument, make standards (the asset-holding standards) that deal with the following in relation to each digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform issued by one or more financial services licensees:
the activities or conduct of the licensees, or of the authorised representatives of the licensees, in relation to:
possessing and safeguarding the underlying assets of the platforms; or
recordkeeping, reconciliation and reporting for the underlying assets of the platforms; or
using the underlying assets of the platforms;

the provision by the licensees of supplementary services relating to the underlying assets of the platforms, including services concerning fund accounting, compliance monitoring, performance reporting, and tax;
any matter prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph.
Note 1: An asset includes a right (see section 9AB).
Note 2: Different standards may apply to different classes of assets (see subsection 33(3A) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901).
In considering whether to make a standard under subsection (1), ASIC must be reasonably satisfied that the proposed standard:

is adequate, effective and appropriate for all digital asset platforms and tokenised custody platforms, including by being reasonably proportionate for differences in the size, scale or nature of such platforms; and

requires any money held under a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform (that is not an underlying asset of the platform) to be held in trust for, or on behalf of, a client under the platform; and
provides to the operator of:
a digital asset platform; or
a tokenised custody platform;
options for holding money for or on behalf of a client under the platform, to assist the operator to mitigate the impacts of a bank refusing to provide services ordinarily provided by a bank; and
does not prohibit a licensee who issues a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform from:
providing particular services; or
arranging for particular services to be provided;
to clients under the platform; and
does not prohibit a licensee who issues a digital asset platform, or a tokenised custody platform, from possessing digital tokens under the platform:
in one address or location on public digital token infrastructure or similar infrastructure; or
in one wallet;
if the licensee’s internal accounting system identifies the digital tokens as the client’s; and
includes any requirement or limitation, or achieves any outcome, prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph.

section.heading: Transactional and settlement standards

content.p: (1) ASIC may, by legislative instrument, make standards (the transactional and settlement standards) dealing with:
the conduct of persons in relation to the underlying assets of:
digital asset platforms; or
tokenised custody platforms;
issued by financial services licensees; and
any matter prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph.
For the purposes of (but without limiting) subsection (1), the conduct the standards can deal with includes the following:
facilitating acquisitions, disposals, encumbrances or settlements of the underlying assets of a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform;
matched principal trading and other execution models that involve the intermediary facilitation of such transactions;

handling, prioritising and executing the instructions of a client under such a platform (including across different business models such as market operation, market making, liquidity provision, brokerage, or dealing);

the conduct of persons engaged by the issuer of such a platform in relation to the performance of a function in any of the above paragraphs (including the conduct of authorised representatives, agents and subcontractors).
In considering whether to make a standard under subsection (1), ASIC must be reasonably satisfied that the proposed standard:

is adequate, effective and appropriate for all digital asset platforms and tokenised custody platforms, including by being reasonably proportionate for differences in the size, scale or nature of such platforms; and
allows for a client under such a platform to direct the exercise, for or on the client’s behalf, of specified rights that:
relate to the underlying assets of the platform; and
are provided under the platform; and
does not prevent the issuer of such a platform from sourcing liquidity from platforms operating:
outside of this jurisdiction; and
with or without a licence under this Act; and
requires the issuer of such a platform to:
enter into an enforceable written arrangement with each person providing liquidity to, or pursuing market-making strategies through, the platform; and
monitor the activities or conduct of that person under the arrangement; and
enforce the arrangement; and
includes any requirement or limitation, or achieves any outcome, prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph.

section.heading: Platform rules of a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform

content.p: Content of the platform rules
The platform rules of a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform issued by a financial services licensee must include:
transparent and non-discriminatory eligibility criteria for identifying who can become a client under the platform; and
any ongoing obligations of a client under the platform; and
(c) the method (the settlement method) for executing client instructions to execute and settle transactions involving the acquisition or disposal of underlying assets of the platform; and
a requirement for the licensee to disclose to a potential client under the platform:
the settlement method for transactions involving the acquisition or disposal of underlying assets of the platform; and

whether external liquidity sources will be used in relation to such transactions and, if so, the extent to which the licensee remains responsible for the execution and settlement of such transactions; and
who bears any counterparty or operational risk during execution and settlement of such transactions; and
how any changes to the settlement method will be communicated to clients; and
whether and how a client’s acquisition of an underlying asset of the platform will be recorded in any legal or technical register; and
any other matter prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this subparagraph; and
information about the types of assets that are or will be available as underlying assets of the platform; and
the method for how the licensee, or any custodian of the platform, will determine what assets are or will be available as underlying assets of the platform; and
the arrangements for depositing, redeeming and directing the delivery of underlying assets in their actual form (rather than their money’s worth); and
any other rules prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this subsection.
Note: The licensee must comply with this provision as it is part of the financial services law (see paragraph 912A(1)(c)).
Legal effect of the platform rules
The platform rules of a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform have effect as a contract under seal:
between the licensee and each client under the platform; and
if, under the platform, clients can have dealings with each other—between a client under the platform and each other client under the platform;

under which each of those persons agrees to observe the platform rules to the extent that they apply to the person and to engage in conduct that the person is required by the platform rules to engage in.
Note: A failure to comply with the platform rules may be a breach of an implied warranty (see section 12ED of the ASIC Act).
However, if there is an inconsistency between the platform rules of the platform, and any of the following other instruments:
the transactional and settlement standards;
an instrument of a kind prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph;
those other instruments prevail over the platform rules to the extent of the inconsistency.

section.heading: Prohibition by the Minister—transactions etc. involving certain financial products must not happen through digital asset platforms or tokenised custody platforms

content.p: Prohibition
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, declare that conduct involving a specified financial product must not happen through:
a specified digital asset platform; or
a specified tokenised custody platform;
if one or more of the financial services authorised by an Australian financial services licence relate to the issuing of the platform.
Note 1: Such a licensee must comply with this prohibition (see section 912BD).

Note 2: The Minister could, for example, declare that a particular class of financial products must not be held as underlying assets of a particular digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform.
Note 3: A declaration may:
declare one or more classes of conduct; or
specify one or more (or all) classes of financial products or platforms;
(see subsection 13(3) of the Legislation Act 2003).
Note 4: In making a declaration, the Minister must have regard to the matters in subsection 912BI(1).
The prohibition may apply:
unconditionally or subject to specified conditions; and
(b) for a specified period or indefinitely (the prohibition duration).
Varying or revoking a prohibition
The Minister may, at any time by legislative instrument, make a declaration:
varying a prohibition declared under subsection (1) to:
impose conditions, or additional conditions, on the prohibition; or
vary or revoke any of the conditions on the prohibition; or
extend or shorten the prohibition duration (including as affected by any variation from a previous operation of this subparagraph); or
revoking a prohibition declared under subsection (1).
However, the Minister may only take action under subsection (3) after:
giving notice, and an opportunity to make submissions on the proposed action, to each financial services licensee known by the Minister to be covered by the prohibition; and
both:

the Minister has caused a notice to be published on ASIC’s website allowing a reasonable period within which each financial services licensee covered by the prohibition may make submissions on the proposed action; and
that period has ended.

section.heading: Prohibition by the Minister—matters to which the Minister has regard

content.p: In considering whether to make a declaration under subsection 912BH(1) or (3) prohibiting conduct in relation to one or more financial products, the Minister must have regard to:
the likely effect on the Australian economy, and on the efficiency, integrity and stability of the Australian financial system; and
any impact on the provision of digital asset platforms or tokenised custody platforms (as applicable); and
the likely regulatory impact; and
whether the conduct or financial products have resulted, or will or are likely to result, in significant consumer detriment; and
any relevant advice the Minister has received under subsection (3).
The Minister may also have regard to any other matters that the Minister considers relevant.
ASIC, APRA or Reserve Bank may advise the Minister
ASIC, APRA or the Reserve Bank may (on its own initiative) and must (at the request of the Minister):
consider whether a declaration under subsection 912BH(1) or (3) should be made; and
advise the Minister accordingly.
Omit “or 912B”, substitute “, 912B, 912BB, 912BC or 912BD”.

division.heading: Disclosure framework for digital asset platforms and tokenised custody platforms

section.heading: Scope of this Division

content.p: This Division applies in relation to a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform only if the platform is issued, or will be issued, by a financial services licensee in the course of a financial services business.

section.heading: Giving a DAP/TCP Guide before issuing a platform

content.p: Giving the Guide before issuing a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform to a person as a retail client
The licensee must, before issuing a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform to a person as a retail client under the platform, give the person a DAP/TCP Guide that:
includes the information required by section 1020AO for the platform; and
is written and presented in a clear, concise and effective manner.
Note 1: The Guide can consist of 2 or more documents if they are presented and given in a way that satisfies paragraphs (a) and (b).
Note 2: This subsection is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).
Guide is no longer accurate
The licensee must not give a person a DAP/TCP Guide if the licensee becomes aware that:
a material change has occurred to the information in it; or
it has become misleading or deceptive or likely to mislead or deceive.
To avoid doubt, the licensee must still comply with subsection (1).
Note: This subsection is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).
Circumstances affecting accuracy of Guides that have been given
If:
(a) the licensee gives a person a DAP/TCP Guide (the existing Guide) in accordance with subsection (1); but
a new circumstance later arises so that the Guide no longer includes the information required by section 1020AO for the platform;
the licensee must, as soon as practicable after the new circumstance arises, give the person:
updated information to enable the person to again readily have the information required by section 1020AO for the platform; and
objective advice about whether the updated information is, when compared with the information in the existing Guide, materially adverse to a retail client under the platform.
Note 1: The updated information could take the form of a “Supplementary DAP/TCP Guide”, and could include information about how to readily access particular information on a website.
Note 2: For paragraph (b), examples of a new circumstance include the licensee becoming aware of the matters in paragraph (2)(a) or (b).
Note 3: This subsection is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).

section.heading: Content of a DAP/TCP Guide

content.p: A DAP/TCP Guide must include all information a person would reasonably require for the purposes of making a decision, as a retail client, whether to become a client under the platform, including such information that the person would reasonably require to:
understand the nature of the platform and any risks associated with participation in the platform; and
identify:
the licensee (as the issuer of the platform); and
any custodians of the platform; and
the nature of the responsibilities of the issuer and of any custodians, and of the relationships between them; and
understand the method and extent of all charges associated with the platform, including any right of the issuer or any other person to recoup expenses from a client’s assets; and

understand any differences between the rights of a client under the platform and the rights of a person who (directly) holds an underlying asset of the platform, including information on any applicable:
cooling-off rights; and
voting rights; and
withdrawal rights under section 724 or 1016E; and
understand how and to whom a client may make a complaint in relation to:
the operation of the platform; and
the underlying assets of the platform (where this is possible); and
financial product advice provided to the client in relation to the platform that is not provided by or on behalf of the licensee; and
understand a client’s rights to disclosure in relation to the underlying assets of the platform, including that a client may elect to receive copies of communications relating to those assets that:
are sent to the holders of those assets; or
the holders of those assets may elect to receive; and
understand how the licensee, or any custodians of the platform, determine what is or will be available as underlying assets of the platform; and
understand any other matters prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph.
A DAP/TCP Guide must also include:
a statement that copies of the platform’s voting policy are available free on request; and
a statement to the effect that the total fees and expenses payable by a client will include the costs of the platform; and
a statement to the effect that the fees and expenses for any conduct that:
can be engaged in under the platform; and
is chosen by the client to be engaged in;
will be in addition to the fees charged for the platform; and
examples, based on estimates, of the fees and expenses referred to in paragraphs (b) and (c), that satisfy any requirements prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph; and
anything else prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph.
Despite subsection (1), that subsection does not require a DAP/TCP Guide to include publicly-available information, provided that the DAP/TCP Guide:
refers to the information; and
includes sufficient details about the information to enable a person to easily identify and locate it; and
states that the information can be obtained free from the licensee on request; and
if any of the information is about any significant benefits to which a person will or may become entitled under the platform—includes a summary of that information; and
if any of the information is about any significant risks associated with the platform—includes a summary of those risks.

section.heading: Having and administering a platform voting policy

content.p: (1) The licensee must, before issuing a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform to a person as a retail client under the platform, ensure that there is a policy (the voting policy) for the platform that:
deals with the exercise of any voting or governance rights arising for:
the underlying assets of the platform; and
any other asset that is otherwise held or possessed through the platform; and
includes the information required by section 1020AQ for the platform; and
is written and presented in a clear, concise and effective manner.
Note: This subsection is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).
The licensee must ensure that the voting policy:
is kept accurate; and
is administered for the platform by the licensee or by a custodian of the platform.
Note: This subsection is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).
The regulations may prescribe how liability is to be dealt with for proxy voting relating to an asset of a kind covered by paragraph (1)(a).

section.heading: Content of a platform’s voting policy

content.p: A platform’s voting policy must:
identify any rights a client under the platform will have in relation to any voting or governance rights arising for:
each underlying asset of the platform; and
any other asset that is otherwise held or possessed through the platform;
for the client (whether directly or through a nominee); and
(b) state whether a client under the platform may instruct the licensee, or a custodian of the platform, (the authority) about the exercise of any such voting or governance rights; and
if the client may give such instructions:
require the authority to vote only when, and as, instructed by the client (including under a standing instruction); and

require clients to be given, as soon as practicable, copies of any relevant information received by the licensee or a custodian in relation to the assets that are the subject of the voting or governance rights; and
identify how copies of this relevant information are to be given to clients; and
identify the steps that are to be taken after voting instructions have been communicated by a client to the authority; and
identify whether any costs are to be charged to the client for exercising voting or governance rights; and
if the client may not give such instructions—require the authority not to exercise any such voting or governance rights; and
state how any regulations made for the purposes of subsection 1020AP(3) (about proxy voting) relate to any such voting or governance rights.

section.heading: Disclosure obligations for underlying assets etc. of platforms

content.p: Giving copies of communications about related assets
If:
(a) a financial product, or a prescribed digital token, (the asset):
is an underlying asset of a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform; or
is otherwise held or possessed through such a platform;
for a client under the platform (whether directly or through a nominee); and
communications are required by law to be given to the person who holds or possesses the asset (including communications required to be given on request);

the licensee who issues the platform must, on request, ensure the client is given a copy of such communications as soon as practicable after the communications are received by the licensee or by a custodian of the platform.
Note 1: The platform needs to be one that is issued, or will be issued, by a financial services licensee in the course of a financial services business (see section 1020AM).
Note 2: This subsection is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).
The client’s request may be for a particular communication, or may be a standing request for one or more classes of such communications.
Disclosure requirements relating to acquisitions of prescribed digital tokens

Regulations made for the purposes of this subsection may prescribe disclosure obligations before an acquisition of a prescribed digital token, by way of issue or sale, happens because of an instruction given:
under a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform; and
by a client under the platform (whether directly or through a nominee).
Without limiting subsection (3), such obligations could be imposed on one or more of the following:
the licensee who issues the platform;
a custodian of the platform;
a person who is to issue or sell the prescribed digital token.
Note: The platform needs to be one that is issued, or will be issued, by a financial services licensee in the course of a financial services business (see section 1020AM).
A person must comply with an obligation imposed on the person by regulations made for the purposes of subsection (3).
Note: This subsection is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).
Definitions
In this section:
prescribed digital token means a digital token that:
is not a financial product; and
is of a class prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph.

section.heading: Meaning of public digital token infrastructure

content.p: (1) Public digital token infrastructure means any software, hardware, or combination of software or hardware, (the infrastructure):
that is used for transmitting, processing, or recording:
electronic records that are digital tokens; or
electronic records relating to digital tokens; and
for which subsection (2) or (3) applies.
This subsection applies if all of the following are satisfied for certain protocols that apply to the infrastructure:
the protocols are a set of open source and publicly accessible standards for transmitting, processing and recording electronic records in a non-discretionary manner;

the protocols permit any person to contribute to the integrity, functionality and reliability of the infrastructure by conducting activities involving transmitting, processing and recording such electronic records;
the protocols are not reliant on any participant having a role so critical that the transmitting, processing, or recording of such electronic records cannot happen without the participant;
no regulations are made for the purposes of this paragraph to prescribe that this subsection does not apply for the protocols.
This subsection applies for the infrastructure if it is prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this subsection.

section.heading: Meaning of custodial staking arrangement

content.p: (1) A custodial staking arrangement, for a digital asset platform or a tokenised custody platform, is an arrangement that:
is entered into by the operator of the platform and by a beneficiary under the platform (whether directly or through a nominee); and
is entered into through the facility that constitutes the platform; and

(c) permits the operator to allow one or more of the underlying assets possessed under the platform for the beneficiary (whether directly or through a nominee) to be used for activities (consensus activities) described in paragraph 9E(2)(b) if:
the beneficiary; or
the nominee;
expressly authorises the operator to do so; and
ensures that rewards from the consensus activities, after deducting any fees and charges, are passed on to the beneficiary (whether directly or through a nominee); and
may benefit the beneficiary in one or more of the following ways:
by allowing the underlying assets to be returned earlier than if the beneficiary had participated in consensus activities directly;
by allowing the underlying assets to be used in consensus activities if the beneficiary would otherwise have insufficient assets to be able to participate in consensus activities directly;
by protecting the beneficiary from, or by compensating the beneficiary for, any losses arising from the operation of public digital token infrastructure in relation to the underlying assets;
by allowing the beneficiary to pay lower transaction fees than if the beneficiary had participated in consensus activities directly;
a way prescribed by regulations made for the purposes of this subparagraph.
In this section:
beneficiary: a beneficiary under a platform means:
for a digital asset platform—a client under the platform; or
for a tokenised custody platform—a person who possesses a digital token created under the platform by the operator of the platform.

section.heading: Fundraising offers through a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform

content.p: A person who makes an offer of securities:
under a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform; and
that needs disclosure to investors under Part 6D.2; and
that results in the person lodging a disclosure document with ASIC;
must promptly notify the operator of the platform, and each custodian for the platform, if any of the following events happens:
a supplementary or replacement document is lodged with ASIC in relation to the disclosure document;
the person is prohibited under Division 1 of Part 6D.3 from making offers of securities under the disclosure document;
the disclosure document is withdrawn before the expiry date specified in the disclosure document.
Note: This subsection is a civil penalty provision (see section 1317E).
Nothing in Part 6D.2 or 6D.3 requires a disclosure document for offers of securities under a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform to include information about:

part.heading: Transitional provisions relating to the Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026

section.heading: Definitions

content.p: In this Part:
AFSL means an Australian financial services licence.
amended Corporations Act means this Act as in force on commencement.
commencement means the day Schedule 1 to the Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 commences.
Note: This is the day after the end of the 12-month period beginning on the day that Act receives the Royal Assent.
DAP/TCP amendments means the amendments made by Schedule 1 to the Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026.
DAP/TCP financial service means a financial service relating to: a digital asset platform; or a tokenised custody platform.
a digital asset platform; or
a tokenised custody platform.
transition period means the 6-month period starting on commencement.

section.heading: Application of amendments to financial services—general

content.p: The DAP/TCP amendments apply in relation to a DAP/TCP financial service to the extent that the service is provided on or after commencement.

section.heading: Transitional—delay in how amendments apply for AFSLs

content.p: (1) Despite section 1731, the DAP/TCP amendments do not apply in relation to the provision of a DAP/TCP financial service at any time during the transition period while the following person (the responsible person):
if the person providing the service is doing so not as an agent or representative of any other person—the person providing the service;
otherwise—the person on whose behalf the service is being provided;
does not hold an AFSL that is subject to a condition authorising the provision of the service.
Note: This subsection applies if the responsible person:
does not hold an AFSL at all; or
holds an AFSL that authorises only the provision of other services.
However:
during the transition period, the responsible person may apply under the amended Corporations Act for ASIC to decide whether or not to:
grant the responsible person an AFSL that is subject to a condition authorising the provision of the service; or
vary the conditions on the responsible person’s AFSL to authorise the provision of the service; and
ASIC may make such a decision under the amended Corporations Act in response to the application.

Despite section 1731, if the responsible person applies as described in paragraph (2)(a) of this section, the DAP/TCP amendments do not apply in relation to the provision of the service until the day after the day ASIC makes a decision described in that paragraph in response to the application.
Note: If the responsible person fails to apply during the transition period, then the DAP/TCP amendments will start to apply immediately after the transition period.

section.heading: Application of amendments otherwise than in connection with financial services

content.p: If a provision of the amended Corporations Act:
relates to a digital asset platform or tokenised custody platform; but
does not relate to the platform in connection with a financial service;
then the DAP/TCP amendments of that provision apply in relation to the platform only if the platform is, or is to be, issued on or after commencement.

section.heading: Acquisition of property

content.p: Despite section 1350, sections 1731 to 1733 do not apply, and are taken never to have applied, to the extent that their operation would result in an acquisition of property from a person otherwise than on just terms.
(2) In subsection (1), acquisition of property and just terms have the same meanings as in paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.

section.heading: Regulations

content.p: The regulations may make provisions of a transitional, application or saving nature relating to this Part and the amendments and repeals made by the amending Schedule.
Without limiting subsection (1), regulations made for the purpose of that subsection may modify provisions of this Act.
